defaults._fit_mode_help: ideal: cut each platform's variant into its ideal_range when the material allows; limits: only enforce min/max_duration
defaults._placement_help: platform: every platform gets its own render built to its own spec (safe zones, encode, loudness); universal: one render that satisfies the strictest of every selected platform's spec

youtube_shorts.label: YouTube Shorts
youtube_shorts.notes: Up to 3 min counts as a Short (vertical or square) since Oct 2024, but completion rate drops past ~60 s; keep most under a minute. Put #Shorts in the title or description and front-load the keyword.
youtube_shorts.spec_notes: Vertical or square, up to 3 min. Title and channel strip occupy the bottom ~20%; action rail on the right ~12%. #Shorts in title or description.

instagram_reels.label: Instagram Reels
instagram_reels.notes: 3 min is the widely available cap (20 min for some accounts). 15-45 s performs best; the first line of the caption is the hook. 3-5 niche hashtags beat 30 generic ones.
instagram_reels.spec_notes: Meta recommends 30 fps and keeping the top 14% and bottom ~22% clear (caption/comment bar). 4 GB cap; 1080x1920 H.264/AAC.

tiktok.label: TikTok
tiktok.notes: 10 min uploads are safe everywhere (longer for some accounts). 21-34 s is the engagement sweet spot; Creator Rewards needs 60 s+. The caption doubles as the title, so keep the hook in the first 60 chars.
tiktok.spec_notes: 287.6 MB is the iOS app cap (web and API allow 4 GB). Right action rail ~15%, bottom caption/music strip ~18%, 23-60 fps, H.264/AAC MP4.

facebook_reels.label: Facebook Reels
facebook_reels.notes: Meta lifted the 90 s cap in 2025; 3 min is a safe ceiling. 15-30 s performs best with an older audience; plainer language, fewer hashtags, lead with the payoff.
facebook_reels.spec_notes: Same family as Reels but the Facebook nav bar eats a little more of the bottom (~24%). 30 fps recommended, 4 GB cap.
